title: VB.NET Module exposes public shared state and procedures — migrate to C# static class, exposing hidden global state
sourceContent:
' VB.NET Module — equivalent to a C# sealed static class in most ways,
' BUT members are directly accessible without qualification inside the
' same assembly. This implicit-import behaviour has NO equivalent in C#.
' Any C# file that uses these members must qualify them with the class name.
Module AppGlobals
    ' Module-level variable: shared across the entire process lifetime.
    ' Maps to a C# static field — exposes process-wide mutable state.
    Public CurrentUserId As String = "anonymous"
    Public RequestCount As Integer = 0

    ' Sub in a Module = public static void method in C#.
    Public Sub IncrementRequest()
        RequestCount += 1
    End Sub

    ' Function returning a computed value from the mutable state.
    Public Function GetSummary() As String
        Return $"User={CurrentUserId}, Requests={RequestCount}"
    End Function
End Module

' Calling code — note no qualification needed in VB.NET:
' IncrementRequest()   -- works without AppGlobals.IncrementRequest()
' Dim s = GetSummary() -- works without AppGlobals.GetSummary()
'
' In C#, every call site must be updated to:
' AppGlobals.IncrementRequest();
' var s = AppGlobals.GetSummary();
'
' Module-level variables that accumulate state across requests
' are almost certainly bugs in a multi-threaded ASP.NET Core app.
notes: VB.NET Modules are the closest equivalent to C# static classes, but they differ in one critical way: members are implicitly imported and callable without qualification anywhere in the assembly. C# has no such mechanism — every call site must be updated to prefix the class name. More importantly, module-level mutable variables (Public X As Integer) become static fields on the C# class. In a Framework Web Forms app these were reset on each AppPool recycle; in ASP.NET Core running on .NET 10 under Kestrel they are never reset between requests, meaning they accumulate state for the lifetime of the process. This is a common source of subtle concurrency bugs in migrated apps. The spec must enumerate every mutable module variable and flag them as potential sideEffect / openQuestion for refactoring to injected services.
